page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, full width. Running head at top with title and year on the left and page number on the right. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: mos[?] Scotorum arma expedientium, ex colle edito speculatus, discessum fugæ similem majori
quam venisset gradu accelerat; Scoti vero milites gregarii qui
ex confuso reditu trepidationem adversi agminis ex
propinquo aspiciebant, Anglos hostiliter urgere ve-
hementer cupiebant, & ægre certe à tribunis & præ-
fectis suis contineri in suis stationibus potuerunt, qui
cum ad propulsandam non inferendam injuriam ar-
ma suos induisse meminissent, extra limites innocuæ
tutelæ in hoc primo belli tentamento progredien-
dum non censuerunt, & confessionem hanc timoris
ipsa victoria haud inferiorem judicarunt: præsertim
cum ingenue postea agnoverint Angli, penes Scotos
fuisse, si hostili in ipsos animo fuissent, indecorum
satis reditum efficere potuisse.
Frustrata hac expeditione, non dubium erat An-
glos, si qua esset ex tali discessu contracta ignomi-
nia, statim reparaturos; rumor etiam fuit eos totis
viribus illud moliri; quare postridie illius diei, 5.vid.
Iunii Generalis Leslius copias illas Kalsone evocat &
ut sibi ad collem Dunsianum medio fere itinere oc-
currerent, jussit: Etenim cum satis prodidissent An-
gli expeditione illa in Kalsonem, propositum sibi es-
se Scotiam invadere, castra propius Angliam pro-
movet Leslius, & ad collem Dunsianum (vulgo Duns
Law, Dunsio municipio in Mercia propinquum;
quod nativitate Iohannis Scoti Subtilis, & ludi-
briosa Henrici Percii Northumbriæ Comitis per
pastorum crepitacula, fuga anno 1374. insigne est)
sex millibus passuum ab Anglia distantem, unde pro-
spectus esset in castra regia, posita ad alteram Tuedę
ripam, loco editiori castra metatur. Ad primum Sco-
torum adventum Anglis prorsus inexspectatum, ad
arma clamatum est in castris regiis: Nam licet an-
tea ex profugarum Scotorum relationibus, qui apud
eos commeabāt, audivissent Angli, Scotos ex adverso

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the first word of the page appears as "tnos", most likely "mos" with a damaged first letter, marked [?]. "Tuedę" is uncertain and may be "Tuedæ". The signature "A a 2" is read from a faint mark at the foot. The catchword "consistere" is read from "confistere" with the long s normalised. The page number and the year in the running head are as printed.
